html:
The Arikapú are a very small Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, from the upper Branco River, a tributary of the Guaporé. Their language belongs to the Yabutian family, a branch of the Macro-Jê languages, and today has only two speakers.

Like their neighbours they were struck by the rubber boom and by disease in the early 1900s, and the survivors were moved to the Rio Branco Indigenous Land, where they live alongside other peoples. A dictionary of about 1,350 words has been made to record the language.
